title: A Orchard for the Garden
premise: Freya Sterling keeps her grandmother's lighthouse on the Cornish coast and writes romance novels under a pseudonym, convinced love only works for people with better timing. When a local literary festival pairs anonymous pen-pals, she's matched with Callum Reeve, the developer whose family plans to buy and demolish the lighthouse—and neither realizes at first who is on the other end of the letters. As their written intimacy deepens while their real-world rivalry sharpens, Freya must choose between protecting her home and trusting the man who could destroy it. In the end, Callum publicly abandons the development, the lighthouse becomes a writers' retreat run by their found community of festival friends, and Freya finally lets someone stay after the last train leaves.
about_author: Jude Yarrow is the pen name of a former bookseller who spent a decade recommending other people's love stories before writing one of her own. She lives near the sea, where she collects tide-worn glass and insists every letter deserves an answer.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the eve of the Penhallow Literary Festival, Freya closes up the lighthouse and watches the last train leave without her—again—while drafting rejection-proof excuses to skip the festival's anonymous pen-pal program. Her grandmother's old letters hint she once had a correspondent of her own. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: Enemies by Post
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The festival pairs Freya with 'C,' a stranger who defends developers over tea-shop owners in his first letter; meanwhile, in person, she clashes publicly with Callum Reeve over his family's plan to purchase the lighthouse headland. Neither connects the two men. Emotional beat: sparks of antagonism in both worlds.

chapters.title: What the Light Keeps
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum tours the lighthouse under pretense of inspection and is unsettled by how alive it feels—and by Freya's fierce, unguarded defense of it. That night he writes 'F' that some places shouldn't be sold, surprising himself. Emotional beat: first hairline crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: Ink and Salt
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Letters deepen into confessions: 'C' admits he never chose his family's business, echoing what Freya's late mother gave up for duty. At a festival reading, Freya and Callum argue about legacy so heatedly that friends notice the chemistry underneath. Emotional beat: intimacy growing where they can't see it.

chapters.title: The Found Ones
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. Festival misfits—retired teacher Maren, teenage volunteer Dev, and bookseller Priya—adopt both Freya and Callum into late-night kitchen-table dinners, becoming the found family neither expected. Callum begins quietly delaying the development survey. Emotional beat: belonging sneaking past defenses.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. A storm forces Callum to shelter at the lighthouse; he and Freya share whiskey, griefs, and an almost-kiss interrupted by a distress flare he helps her answer. He writes 'F' that he met someone who makes him want to be braver than his name allows. Emotional beat: desire tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the festival's letter-reading gala, handwriting on a displayed page betrays Callum as 'C'—and his firm's demolition timeline is announced the same night. Feeling doubly betrayed, Freya flees into the storm-lashed dark. Emotional beat: climax of betrayal; loyalty to place versus truth about the man.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum finds Freya's unsent replies and her grandmother's letters revealing the development would erase a century of saved lives. He confronts his father, risks disinheritance, and drafts one final letter Freya refuses to read. Emotional beat: choosing truth over duty at personal cost.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the festival's final night, Callum publicly withdraws the purchase and reads his last letter aloud from the lighthouse gallery as the crowd below holds its breath. Freya, watching the last train depart empty, chooses to stay—and lets him stay too. Emotional beat: climax resolving into surrender to love.

chapters.title: An Orchard for the Garden
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue tone. Spring: the lighthouse reopens as a writers' retreat tended by their found family, an orchard planted where the fence once divided them. Freya finishes her novel, dedicating it to 'the stranger who wrote back.' Emotional beat: second chances, finally well-timed.
